title.es: Cómo se construye un segmento de pódcast

es: Reconocer marcadores del discurso oral (anyway, by the way, as I was saying, to sum up, before we go) y saber si abren, cambian de tema, resumen o cierran.

teaching.en: The host opens the segment: «Welcome back to the show. To begin with, our topic is sleep.»
teaching.es: El presentador abre el segmento: «Bienvenidos de nuevo al programa. Para empezar, nuestro tema es el sueño.»
teaching.explanationEs: Welcome back y to begin with abren el segmento y presentan el tema.
segments: The host opens the segment: «Welcome back to the
show. To begin with, our topic is sleep.»
teaching.audioText: The host opens the segment: «Welcome back to the show. To begin with, our topic is sleep.»

teaching.en: «Anyway» and «moving on» are markers that change the topic.
teaching.es: «Bueno» y «pasando a otra cosa» son marcadores que cambian de tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Anyway y moving on cierran una idea y abren otra; se colocan al principio, con coma.
segments: «Anyway» and «moving on» are
markers that change the topic.
teaching.audioText: «Anyway» and «moving on» are markers that change the topic.

teaching.en: «By the way, our guest wrote a book» adds a small extra idea.
teaching.es: «Por cierto, nuestro invitado escribió un libro» añade una pequeña idea extra.
teaching.explanationEs: By the way = por cierto: sale un momento del tema principal para dar un dato.
segments: «By the way, our guest wrote a
book» adds a small extra idea.
teaching.audioText: «By the way, our guest wrote a book» adds a small extra idea.

teaching.en: «As I was saying, sleep matters» brings the topic back after an interruption.
teaching.es: «Como iba diciendo, el sueño importa» devuelve el tema tras una interrupción.
teaching.explanationEs: As I was saying = como iba diciendo: retoma una idea que se había interrumpido.
segments: «As I was saying, sleep matters» brings
the topic back after an interruption.
teaching.audioText: «As I was saying, sleep matters» brings the topic back after an interruption.

teaching.en: «So, to sum up» and «in short» introduce a summary of the episode.
teaching.es: «Así que, en resumen» y «en pocas palabras» introducen un resumen del episodio.
teaching.explanationEs: To sum up e in short resumen lo dicho; so también puede abrir una conclusión.
segments: «So, to sum up» and «in short»
introduce a summary of the episode.
teaching.audioText: «So, to sum up» and «in short» introduce a summary of the episode.

teaching.en: «Before we go, thank you for listening» closes the segment.
teaching.es: «Antes de despedirnos, gracias por escuchar» cierra el segmento.
teaching.explanationEs: Before we go y that is all for today cierran el segmento.
segments: «Before we go, thank you
for listening» closes the segment.
teaching.audioText: «Before we go, thank you for listening» closes the segment.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función tiene el marcador del inicio de esta frase?

choices.text: It closes the segment.
It opens the show.
It changes the topic.

feedback.es: Anyway cierra la idea anterior y pasa a la siguiente pregunta: cambia de tema.

hint.es: Piensa en lo que hace el presentador justo después del marcador.

origin.text: «Anyway, let us move on to the next question.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Por cierto, nuestro invitado escribió un libro.»

answer.text: By

feedback.es: By the way introduce un dato extra fuera del hilo principal.

hint.es: Es la preposición que también traduce «por».

origin.text: ___ the way, our guest wrote a book.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Gracias por escuchar y hasta la próxima.»

answer.text: Thank you for listening and see you next time

feedback.es: El cierre agradece al oyente y se despide: thank you for listening and see you next time.

hint.es: Primero se dan las gracias y al final llega la despedida.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del programa con su función.

pairs: Good morning, and welcome to the show.
Anyway, let us look at the next question.
In short, sleep matters.
Until next time, take care.

feedback.es: Cada marcador cumple una función en el segmento: abrir, cambiar de tema, resumir o cerrar.

pairs: Good morning, and welcome to the show.
Anyway, let us look at the next question.
In short, sleep matters.
Until next time, take care.

prompt.es: ¿Qué hace la presentadora con «as I was saying»?

choices.text: She goes back to an idea after an interruption.
She says goodbye to the listeners.
She changes to a completely new topic.

feedback.es: As I was saying significa «como iba diciendo»: retoma una idea que se había interrumpido.

origin.text: «As I was saying, three tips are enough for today.»

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés: «Así que, en resumen, el invitado da tres consejos.»

answer.text: So, to sum up, the guest gives three tips.
accepted: So, to sum up, the guest gives three tips.
To sum up, the guest gives three tips.
So, to sum up, our guest gives three tips.

feedback.es: To sum up introduce el resumen del segmento; so puede acompañarlo al inicio.

origin.text: Quieres resumir lo que dijo el invitado en el segmento.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que hace la presentadora en estas frases.

choices.text: She opens the episode and introduces a guest.
She closes the episode and thanks the guest.
She changes to a new topic.

feedback.es: That is all for today es un marcador de cierre: termina el episodio y agradece al invitado.

origin.audio: That is all for today. Thank you to our guest for joining us.

prompt.es: ¿Qué marcador introduce el resumen de este segmento?

choices.text: Anyway
To begin with
In short

feedback.es: In short resume lo dicho; anyway cambia de tema y to begin with abre el segmento.

origin.text: To begin with, let us define the topic. Anyway, our guest will give three examples. In short: sleep and mood are linked.

prompt.es: Completa tres marcadores de un segmento de pódcast.

answer.text: Welcome | Moving | Before

feedback.es: Welcome back abre, moving on cambia de tema y before we go cierra el segmento.

sentences: ___ on, let us hear our guest.
___ we go, here is one last tip.
origin.text: Traducción: «Bienvenidos de nuevo al programa.» «Pasando a otra cosa, escuchemos a nuestro invitado.» «Antes de despedirnos, aquí tienes un último consejo.»

prompt.es: Escribe en inglés: «Pasando a otro tema, hablemos de las pantallas.»

answer.text: Moving on, let us talk about screens.
accepted: Moving on, let us talk about screens.
Anyway, let us talk about screens.
Moving on, let us talk about the screens.

feedback.es: Moving on y anyway cambian de tema: van al principio, con coma, y no se combinan con but.

origin.text: Quieres cambiar de tema en tu segmento de pódcast.

prompt.es: ¿Qué función cumple «To begin with» en este segmento?

choices.text: It starts the first part of the talk.
It says goodbye to the audience.
It summarises what was said.

feedback.es: To begin with significa «para empezar»: abre la primera parte de la charla.

origin.text: «To begin with, let us look at the facts.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Como iba diciendo, el tema es importante.»

answer.text: As I was saying the topic is important

feedback.es: As I was saying retoma la idea interrumpida antes de continuar.

prompt.es: Elige la frase con el marcador bien colocado.

choices.text: Anyway, but let us move on.
Anyway, let us move on.
Anyway that let us move on.

feedback.es: Anyway va al principio, con coma, y se une directamente a la idea nueva sin but ni that.

es: Parafrasear y resumir lo que dice otra persona con verbos de habla (claim, point out, admit, suggest, deny, refuse, promise, warn) y su patrón.

teaching.en: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is too much.
teaching.es: Algunos expertos afirman que ocho horas de sueño son demasiadas.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim + that + oración: afirmas algo que otros pueden discutir.
segments: Some experts claim that eight hours
of sleep is too much.
teaching.audioText: Some experts claim that eight hours of sleep is too much.

teaching.en: Critics point out that the study is small, so the summary must be careful.
teaching.es: Los críticos señalan que el estudio es pequeño, así que el resumen debe ser prudente.
teaching.explanationEs: Point out + that: señalas un dato, normalmente para matizar lo que se dijo.
segments: Critics point out that the study is
small, so the summary must be careful.
teaching.audioText: Critics point out that the study is small, so the summary must be careful.

teaching.en: Many people admit checking their phones at night, but some deny doing it.
teaching.es: Mucha gente admite revisar el móvil por la noche, pero algunos niegan hacerlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Admit y deny + -ing: reconocer o negar una acción.
segments: Many people admit checking their phones at
night, but some deny doing it.
teaching.audioText: Many people admit checking their phones at night, but some deny doing it.

teaching.en: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn people not to drink coffee late.
teaching.es: Los médicos sugieren acostarse más temprano y advierten a la gente de que no tome café tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Suggest + -ing; warn + persona + (not) to + verbo.
segments: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they
warn people not to drink coffee late.
teaching.audioText: Doctors suggest going to bed earlier, and they warn people not to drink coffee late.

teaching.en: Some guests refuse to answer, and others promise to reply later.
teaching.es: Algunos invitados se niegan a responder y otros prometen contestar más tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Refuse y promise + to + verbo: negarse o comprometerse a hacer algo.
segments: Some guests refuse to answer, and
others promise to reply later.
teaching.audioText: Some guests refuse to answer, and others promise to reply later.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que resume lo que hace el presentador con este dato.

choices.text: The host points out that the study is small.
The host denies that the study is small.
The host refuses to read the study.

feedback.es: Dar el número de participantes sin discutirlo es señalar un dato: point out + that.

hint.es: Él no niega el dato ni se niega a nada: lo muestra.

origin.text: «The study has only twenty people,» says the host.

prompt.es: Completa: «Ella admitió haber cometido un error.»

answer.text: making

feedback.es: Admit puede ir seguido de un verbo en -ing: admitted making.

hint.es: Después de admit puede ir un verbo en -ing.

origin.text: She admitted ___ a mistake.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El médico sugirió dormir más.»

answer.text: The doctor suggested sleeping more

feedback.es: Suggest se construye con -ing: suggested sleeping.

hint.es: El verbo que sigue a suggested lleva -ing.

prompt.es: Completa las tres frases resumen con el verbo de habla correcto.

answer.text: claims | refused | denied

feedback.es: Afirmar algo discutible es claim + that, negarse a hablar es refuse + to y negar un hecho es deny + -ing.

sentences: The guest ___ that sleep is more important than food.
The boy ___ to tell the truth about the noise.
She ___ taking the money from the box.
origin.text: Traducción: «El invitado afirma que dormir es más importante que comer.» «El chico se negó a decir la verdad sobre el ruido.» «Ella negó haber tomado el dinero de la caja.»

prompt.es: Elige la frase con el patrón correcto para suggest.

choices.text: The host suggested to take a break.
The host suggested taking a break.
The host suggested us to take a break.

feedback.es: Suggest admite -ing o that + oración; las otras dos usan to + verbo, que no es posible con suggest.

prompt.es: Parafrasea en inglés: «Responderé a todos los mensajes», dice la presentadora.

answer.text: The host promises to reply to every message.
accepted: The host promises to reply to every message.
The host promised to reply to every message.
The host promises to reply to all the messages.

feedback.es: Un compromiso de futuro se resume con promise + to + verbo.

origin.text: Frase original: «Responderé a todos los mensajes.» La presentadora lo dice al final del programa.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que hace la doctora con el estudio.

choices.text: She denies that the study exists.
She promises to repeat the study.
She explains that the study is too small to be sure.

feedback.es: Señala que solo participaron veinte estudiantes: un dato que matiza el resultado.

origin.audio: Some experts say that coffee is bad for sleep. But the doctor points out that the study only included twenty students, so the result is not clear.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase resume correctamente lo que dice Leo?

choices.text: Leo admitted forgetting the password.
Leo denied forgetting the password.
Leo warned us about the password.

feedback.es: Pide perdón por haber olvidado la clave: reconoce un error, así que se resume con admit + -ing.

origin.text: LEO: «I forgot the password, sorry.»

prompt.es: Completa tres resúmenes con el patrón correcto.

answer.text: going | to | out

feedback.es: Suggest pide -ing, promise pide to + verbo y point out se escribe con la partícula out antes de that.

sentences: The doctor suggested ___ to bed earlier.
The host pointed ___ that the study was small.
origin.text: Traducción: «El médico sugirió acostarse más temprano.» «Prometieron llamarnos mañana.» «El presentador señaló que el estudio era pequeño.»

prompt.es: Parafrasea en inglés: «No rompí la ventana», dice Ana.

answer.text: Ana denied breaking the window.
accepted: Ana denied that she broke the window.
Ana denied having broken the window.

feedback.es: Negar un hecho propio se resume con deny + -ing o con deny + that + oración.

origin.text: Frase original: «No rompí la ventana.» Ana habla con su profesor.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que resume lo que hace Tom.

choices.text: Tom denies eating the last cake.
Tom admits eating the last cake.
Tom suggests eating the last cake.

feedback.es: Dice que sí se lo comió: reconoce algo incómodo, admit + -ing.

origin.text: TOM: «Yes, I ate the last cake.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los invitados se negaron a responder la pregunta.»

answer.text: The guests refused to answer the question

feedback.es: Refuse + to + verbo: se negaron a responder.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada verbo de habla con lo que expresa.

pairs: claim
point out
warn
refuse

feedback.es: Cada verbo de habla añade una actitud: afirmar, señalar, advertir o negarse.

pairs: claim
point out
warn
refuse

title.en: Take notes from a health segment
title.es: Tomar notas de un segmento de salud

es: Tomar notas de un segmento de audio sobre salud separando la idea principal, los detalles, los ejemplos y la recomendación.

teaching.en: Take a note of the main idea first, and then add the details.
teaching.es: Anota primero la idea principal y después añade los detalles.
teaching.explanationEs: Take a note = anotar: primero lo principal y después lo que lo apoya.
segments: Take a note of the main idea
first, and then add the details.
teaching.audioText: Take a note of the main idea first, and then add the details.

teaching.en: A detail explains the main idea with research, numbers or an example.
teaching.es: Un detalle explica la idea principal con investigaciones, cifras o un ejemplo.
teaching.explanationEs: Los detalles y los ejemplos apoyan la idea principal; no son la idea.
segments: A detail explains the main idea
with research, numbers or an example.
teaching.audioText: A detail explains the main idea with research, numbers or an example.

teaching.en: The main idea of this segment is that a good habit can improve your sleep.
teaching.es: La idea principal de este segmento es que un buen hábito puede mejorar tu sueño.
teaching.explanationEs: La idea principal es lo que el locutor quiere que recuerdes; suele decirse al principio o al final.
segments: The main idea of this segment is that
a good habit can improve your sleep.
teaching.audioText: The main idea of this segment is that a good habit can improve your sleep.

teaching.en: The benefit is more energy, and the risk is tiredness if you stay up late.
teaching.es: El beneficio es más energía y el riesgo es el cansancio si te acuestas tarde.
teaching.explanationEs: Benefit y risk suelen ser detalles: ventajas y peligros que apoyan la idea.
segments: The benefit is more energy, and the risk
is tiredness if you stay up late.
teaching.audioText: The benefit is more energy, and the risk is tiredness if you stay up late.

teaching.en: The speaker's recommendation is simple: put the phone away an hour before bed.
teaching.es: La recomendación del locutor es sencilla: guarda el móvil una hora antes de dormir.
teaching.explanationEs: La recomendación es lo que el locutor te pide que hagas; suele ir al final.
segments: The speaker's recommendation is simple: put the
phone away an hour before bed.
teaching.audioText: The speaker's recommendation is simple: put the phone away an hour before bed.

teaching.en: «For example» introduces an example; it is a detail, not the main idea.
teaching.es: «Por ejemplo» introduce un ejemplo; es un detalle, no la idea principal.
teaching.explanationEs: For example y first, second, also anuncian detalles: no los confundas con la idea principal.
segments: «For example» introduces an example; it is
a detail, not the main idea.
teaching.audioText: «For example» introduces an example; it is a detail, not the main idea.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la idea principal del segmento.

choices.text: Homework is the best way to get better marks.
Good sleep helps students remember what they study.
Students should study more hours every night.

feedback.es: El segmento contradice la idea de que más deberes dan mejores notas y concluye que dormir bien ayuda a recordar.

hint.es: La idea principal suele repetirse al final, tras un «so».

origin.audio: Welcome back to Health Today. Many people think that more homework means better marks. The research says the opposite: students who sleep well remember more. So the message today is simple: sleep is part of studying.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por ejemplo, los adolescentes duermen seis horas.»

answer.text: For

feedback.es: For example introduce un ejemplo, que es un detalle que apoya la idea principal.

hint.es: Es la preposición que también traduce «por».

origin.text: ___ example, teenagers sleep six hours.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La idea principal es que dormir bien ayuda.»

answer.text: The main idea is that sleeping well helps

feedback.es: La idea principal se expresa con The main idea is that + oración.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige un detalle que apoya la idea del segmento.

choices.text: Coffee is better than water in the morning.
Headaches are caused by too much homework.
Water before an exam can make students feel calmer.

feedback.es: El ejemplo final da un detalle concreto: beber agua antes de un examen calma a los estudiantes.

origin.audio: Drinking enough water helps you think. First, it gives you more energy in the morning. Second, it helps you concentrate in class. Third, it stops headaches. For example, students who drink water before an exam often feel calmer.

prompt.es: Elige la nota que es la idea principal de este esquema.

choices.text: Teenagers need more sleep than they get.
Research says most go to bed after midnight.
Advice: keep the same bedtime every day.

feedback.es: La idea principal abarca todo el esquema; la investigación es un detalle y el consejo es la recomendación.

origin.text:
1) Research: most teenagers go to bed after midnight.
2) They sleep six hours; they need nine.
3) Advice: keep the same bedtime every day.
4) Teenagers need more sleep than they get.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada nota con su lugar en el esquema.

pairs: Sleep is part of studying.
For example, six hours is too little.
Put the phone away at ten.

feedback.es: La idea es el mensaje central, el ejemplo apoya con un caso y la recomendación dice qué hacer.

pairs: Sleep is part of studying.
For example, six hours is too little.
Put the phone away at ten.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la recomendación de la doctora.

choices.text: Buy a new phone with a better screen.
Leave the phone outside the bedroom at night.
Sleep two more hours on Sundays.

feedback.es: La doctora aconseja cargar el móvil fuera del dormitorio: esa es la recomendación del segmento.

origin.audio: Many teenagers spend more than four hours a day on their phones. The research shows that this reduces their sleep. The doctor's advice is to charge the phone outside the bedroom and to keep the same bedtime every day.

prompt.es: Completa el esquema con las palabras clave del segmento.

answer.text: sleep | stress | energy | slowly

feedback.es: El esquema recoge la idea (dormir mejor), dos detalles (estrés y energía) y la recomendación (caminar despacio).

sentences: Main idea: a short walk helps you ___ better.
Detail 3: you have more ___ the next day.
Recommendation: walk ___ and avoid hard exercise at night.
origin.text: Transcripción: «A short walk after dinner helps you sleep better. First, it lowers stress. Second, it gives your body time to rest. Third, it gives you more energy the next day. The doctor's advice is simple: walk slowly and do not do hard exercise late at night.»

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el papel de la frase sobre dormir seis horas.

choices.text: It is the main idea of the segment.
It is the recommendation for listeners.
It is a detail that supports the main idea.

feedback.es: Empieza con for example: es un ejemplo que apoya la idea de que una noche corta causa cansancio.

origin.audio: Why do we feel tired in the afternoon? The main reason is a short night. For example, sleeping only six hours can reduce your attention a lot.

prompt.es: Escribe la recomendación del locutor con recommends + -ing.

answer.text: The speaker recommends stopping coffee after noon.
accepted: The speaker recommends stopping coffee after noon.
The speaker recommends not drinking coffee after noon.
The speaker recommends stopping drinking coffee after noon.

feedback.es: La recomendación se resume con recommends + -ing: stopping coffee after noon.

origin.text: Segmento: «Many adults drink coffee after lunch. The research shows that coffee late in the afternoon can delay sleep. So my advice is to stop drinking coffee after noon.»

prompt.es: ¿Qué papel tiene esta frase en un segmento?

choices.text: It gives an example that supports an idea.
It states the recommendation.
It closes the segment.

feedback.es: Here is one case presenta un caso concreto: apoya la idea, no la formula ni cierra el segmento.

origin.text: «Here is one case: walking for ten minutes can improve your mood.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «La recomendación del locutor es dormir siete horas.»

answer.text: The recommendation of the speaker is to sleep seven hours

feedback.es: La recomendación suele ir al final y se expresa con is to + verbo.

prompt.es: Completa: «La investigación dice que los adolescentes duermen poco.»

answer.text: says

feedback.es: Research es incontable y lleva verbo en singular: the research says.

origin.text: The research ___ that teenagers sleep too little.

title.es: Redactar el resumen de un segmento

es: Escribir un resumen fiel de un segmento de audio con tres verbos de habla, según + hablante y la postura de cada participante.

teaching.en: The summary should be faithful: it keeps the main points and does not add new opinions.
teaching.es: El resumen debe ser fiel: mantiene los puntos principales y no añade opiniones nuevas.
teaching.explanationEs: Fiel = cuenta lo que se dijo, no lo que tú piensas.
segments: The summary should be faithful: it keeps the
main points and does not add new opinions.
teaching.audioText: The summary should be faithful: it keeps the main points and does not add new opinions.

teaching.en: According to the guest, phones are useful tools, whereas the host is more cautious.
teaching.es: Según el invitado, los móviles son herramientas útiles, mientras que el presentador es más cauteloso.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + persona atribuye la idea; whereas contrasta dos posturas.
segments: According to the guest, phones are useful
tools, whereas the host is more cautious.
teaching.audioText: According to the guest, phones are useful tools, whereas the host is more cautious.

teaching.en: The guest sounds confident because she claims that a ban does not teach self-control.
teaching.es: La invitada suena segura porque afirma que una prohibición no enseña autocontrol.
teaching.explanationEs: La postura se describe con sounds + adjetivo y se apoya en un verbo de habla.
segments: The guest sounds confident because she claims
that a ban does not teach self-control.
teaching.audioText: The guest sounds confident because she claims that a ban does not teach self-control.

teaching.en: The host raises a concern: too much screen time affects sleep.
teaching.es: El presentador plantea una preocupación: demasiado tiempo de pantalla afecta al sueño.
teaching.explanationEs: Raise a concern = plantear una preocupación.
segments: The host raises a concern: too
much screen time affects sleep.
teaching.audioText: The host raises a concern: too much screen time affects sleep.

teaching.en: A good summary can highlight the stance of each speaker with verbs like claim, admit or warn.
teaching.es: Un buen resumen puede destacar la postura de cada hablante con verbos como claim, admit o warn.
teaching.explanationEs: El verbo de habla ya muestra la actitud: claim afirma, admit concede, warn advierte.
segments: A good summary can highlight the stance of each
speaker with verbs like claim, admit or warn.
teaching.audioText: A good summary can highlight the stance of each speaker with verbs like claim, admit or warn.

teaching.en: Overall, the segment shows that both speakers want the same result: better learning.
teaching.es: En conjunto, el segmento muestra que ambos hablantes quieren el mismo resultado: aprender mejor.
teaching.explanationEs: Overall cierra el resumen con una valoración general.
segments: Overall, the segment shows that both speakers
want the same result: better learning.
teaching.audioText: Overall, the segment shows that both speakers want the same result: better learning.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es un resumen fiel de lo que dicen los dos hablantes?

choices.text: The guest loves phones and the host hates them.
The guest and the host agree that there should be a ban.
The guest thinks a ban is too strict, but the host is not sure.

feedback.es: Recoge lo que dice cada uno sin exagerar: la invitada ve la prohibición demasiado estricta y el presentador duda.

hint.es: Un resumen fiel no exagera ni añade opiniones.

origin.text:
GUEST: «I think a ban is too strict.»
HOST: «I am not sure.»

prompt.es: Completa: «Según la invitada, los móviles son útiles.»

answer.text: According

feedback.es: According to atribuye la idea a una persona sin repetir she thinks.

hint.es: Sirve para atribuir una idea a otra persona.

origin.text: ___ to the guest, phones are useful.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El presentador suena más cauteloso que la invitada.»

answer.text: The host sounds more cautious than the guest

origin.text:
HOST: Welcome back to Tech Talk. Today our topic is phones in the classroom. Our guest is Sara, a teacher and researcher. Sara, should schools ban phones?
GUEST: I do not think so. I claim that a phone is a strong tool: students can search for information, use a dictionary and take notes.
HOST: But many students use their phones to play games or chat with friends.
GUEST: That is true, and I admit that it is a problem. Even so, I suggest using phones only for clear tasks and putting them away when the task is finished.
HOST: Some parents worry that children will become tired and anxious.
GUEST: I understand. The research points out that too much screen time affects sleep, so I warn students not to use their phones late at night.
HOST: I am still not sure. I think a full ban is easier to control.
GUEST: A ban is easy, but it does not teach self-control. I recommend trying a three-month test in one school.
HOST: Interesting. Before we go, thank you, Sara. That is all for today.
